description: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is true for a 50,000-admission multicenter retrospective clinical dataset, but no IRB, ethics committee, approval identifier, or waiver determination is recorded anywhere. The two ethical_reviews entries describe consortium ethics activity (community focus groups, an 'Ethics (Ethical and Trustworthy AI)' pillar, legal-landscape analysis) and their own source_caveats concede that 'the bundle names no IRB, ethics committee, or approval identifier, and does not state that any body performed a formal ethical review of the dataset.'

human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is true but the informed_consent field is entirely absent. For retrospective EHR extraction a waiver of consent is the expected documentation, and neither consent nor waiver is stated.

human_subject_research.special_populations identifies pediatric (PICU) and neonatal (NICU) intensive care patients — classic vulnerable populations — yet at_risk_populations and participant_compensation are both absent, so no protections specific to minors are documented.

status is 'partially released' and updates.update_details describes an actively expanding release (50,000 of an anticipated 100,000 admissions, imaging de-identification and EEG extraction in process), yet no version, version_access, or errata are recorded. A user cannot name or re-obtain the snapshot they analysed.

known_limitations documents pronounced and uneven modality availability (1000 images with de-identification in process, EEG extraction in process, note tokens only), which is a documented missingness pattern, but missing_data_documentation and anomalies are both absent and no imputation_protocols statement is given.

purposes state the goal of developing 'a publicly available, AI-ready critical care dataset', while description, license_and_use_terms and confidential_elements state that all nine modalities are under controlled access conditional on a signed licensing agreement, with one route additionally requiring a '.edu' address. The aspiration and the realised access regime are not reconciled.

regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant is absent although the dataset is derived from US hospital protected health information, and is_deidentified carries no named standard (HIPAA Safe Harbor / Expert Determination) and no identifiers_removed list; its own source_caveats concede the record 'does not state whether identifiable elements remain present in the released dataset'. data_protection_impacts is likewise absent.

No persistent identifier is present. id is 'https://chorus4ai.org/#dataset', a project-website URL with a fragment rather than a DOI, ARK or Handle; doi, citation and rrid are absent, as source_caveats itself records ('no release date, DOI, version identifier, or recommended citation').

Two contact strings are malformed as published and reproduced verbatim: the maintainer email 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu' (domain misspelled, flagged in the record's own source_caveats) and the external resource 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus' recorded without a URL scheme. The notes field also reproduces the site banner misspelling 'repoitory'.

conforms_to_standard collapses three distinct standards (EDF+, Persyst, the OHNLP open source schema) into a single OTHER enum term, and the WFDB term stands for a schema the source describes as extended rather than plain WFDB. The record discloses this, but the structured field understates the standards landscape.

Two sources disagree on scale and the disagreement is carried into the scored values: tier-2 documentation gives 50,000 admissions and 7,642 admissions with radiology data, while the tier-4 August 2025 webinar gives 'over 45K unique admissions' and 1000 images. The record discloses the conflict and unit mismatch rather than concealing it, which is good practice, but the headline counts remain contested.

Temporal coverage of the clinical data is unstated. collection_timeframes gives the NIH award period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 and its own source_caveats notes these 'are the NIH project period for award OT2OD032701, not the clinical period the admissions are drawn from'. Temporal ordering of collection, processing and publication therefore cannot be checked.

No variable-level metadata is present. variables is absent for a release of 1.6 billion OMOP rows across nine modalities; OMOP CDM conformance supplies column semantics for the structured tables only, and nothing describes the flowsheet extensions, the OHNLP token schema, or the waveform channel inventory.

No download_url or platform link is recorded, and no publisher, citation or DOI. Access is reachable only through two personal email addresses in data_governance.access_review_process; the enclave hosting OMOP and telemetry data is described but never named or linked.

No related_datasets or parent_datasets with typed relationships are recorded, even though the dataset is one of four Bridge2AI data generation projects and provisions a sequestered holdout test set that is a sibling of the released cohort.

Contradictory characterization of de-identification. is_deidentified.method records the de-identification type as 'NoDeIdentification' with the explanation that 'no identifiers were collected, so no active de-identification was necessary', while participant_privacy.anonymization_method states that 'Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule was removed from the public release via the Safe Harbor method' and human_subject_research.regulatory_compliance states 'The public release is de-identified under the HIPAA Privacy Rule Safe Harbor method'. Removal of PHI plus removal of sex, race/ethnicity and medications is an active de-identification action, which the 'NoDeIdentification' classification denies.

The dedicated download_url slot is empty even though the dataset is publicly downloadable after self-attestation. The retrieval route is documented only in prose, inside data_governance.access_review_process ('The access route for version 3.0.0 is the FAIRhub access page at https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access').

No software is named in a data-producing or data-transforming role. The record describes format conversions in detail (Topcon .fda to DICOM, Heidelberg FLIO .sdt to DICOM, Garmin .FIT to Open mHealth, Dexcom .csv to Open mHealth, ECG .xml to WFDB, REDCap to OMOP CDM tables) but never names the software that performed them, and no used_software attribute is populated on any preprocessing, cleaning, labeling or imputation entry. The software that is named falls in non-qualifying roles: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application are capture tools, FAIRhub and Microsoft Azure are hosting, and the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard is validation of the released data. The GitHub organization link (https://github.com/AI-READI) is an account root that names no specific tool.

regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is set to 'restricted', which no source states. The record's own source_caveats discloses that the RO-Crate gives 'HL7:2N (normal)' and FAIRhub gives accessType 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired'. 'restricted' is the record's own mapping onto the schema enum, and a reader comparing to the upstream metadata will see a mismatch. The disclosure is exemplary; the residual risk is that the enum value overstates the access barrier for a publicly downloadable dataset.

Unresolved internal conflict on the size of the longitudinal follow-up arm: the FAIRhub healthsheet gives approximately 4% of participants while the FAIRhub README, the RO-Crate and NIH RePORTER give 10% of the cohort. Both figures are carried in collection_timeframes.source_caveats, relationships and known_limitations without resolution.

The accountable institution is stated inconsistently across sources and is surfaced but not resolved: data_governance.accountable_organization and the license name Washington University in St. Louis (ROR 01yc7t268), while the RO-Crate places the principal investigator in the Department of Ophthalmology at the University of Washington, NIH RePORTER lists the University of Washington as awardee, and the IRB is the University of Washington IRB.

sampling_strategies carries two mutually tensioned claims from the same tier 1 source: the healthsheet states the dataset 'contains all possible instances' and answers 'N/A' on sampling strategy, while the FAIRhub study description records the sampling method as 'Non-Probability Sample'. The record reconciles these in prose (the release is not a sample of enrollees, but enrollees are a non-probability sample of the study base), which is semantically correct, but the structured flags is_sample=true / is_representative=false only encode the second reading.

No data_protection_impacts entry and no future_use_impacts entry exist. The absence of a DPIA is disclosed in notes ('no data protection impact analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted'), and anticipated downstream social impact is addressed only indirectly through bias mitigation and the stated motivation for withholding race/ethnicity to prevent stigmatization.

data_governance names a committee (AI-READI Consortium) and an accountable organization but records no committee contact person or address. A general project contact (contact@aireadi.org, https://aireadi.org/contact) and the IRB reliance mailbox (hsdrely@uw.edu) appear elsewhere, so a reader can reach someone, but not the governance body specifically.

Variable metadata is rich in units, measurement technique and reference ranges but carries no external variable identifiers (LOINC, SNOMED, OMOP concept ids) despite the clinical tables being mapped one-to-one onto the OMOP Common Data Model, where such concept ids exist.

Internal contradiction in the de-identification account. is_deidentified.method records the de-identification type as "NoDeIdentification" with the explanation that "no identifiers were collected, so no active de-identification was necessary", yet participant_privacy.anonymization_method states that "Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule was removed from the public release via the Safe Harbor method", is_deidentified.identifiers_removed enumerates removed PHI, sex, race/ethnicity and medications, and human_subject_research.regulatory_compliance states "The public release is de-identified under the HIPAA Privacy Rule Safe Harbor method". Removal by Safe Harbor is an active de-identification operation, so the two accounts cannot both hold. Unlike the six conflicts the record resolves in source_caveats, this one carries no caveat and is presented as settled fact.

Human-subjects / data-protection gate: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is true and the release carries retinal imaging, continuous glucose, wearable and cognitive-test data, but data_protection_impacts is absent as a field. The notes disclose that "no data protection impact analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted". The absence is honestly disclosed rather than concealed, but the artifact itself is missing, which is what Q8's 5-point band requires.

Sustainability claim is undercut by the record's own facts. version_access lists "2.0.0 — DOI 10.60775/fairhub.2 ... no longer accessible" and records that "older versions will not continue to be supported"; related_datasets nevertheless links doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 as an is_new_version_of target. A registered DOI that no longer resolves to accessible content is a persistence failure, not merely a version retirement. The notes add that the FAIRhub landing pages carry the notice "This repository is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives" and that the platform is "currently in beta".

sensitive_elements.sensitive_elements_present is false and confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present is false, while participant_privacy simultaneously records "a theoretical risk of future re-identification", notes that "AI algorithms can infer individual patient characteristics and could facilitate individual-level identification", and documents watermarking, a strict licence and a robust dissemination system as deterrents. Declaring no sensitive elements while deploying anti-re-identification controls over retinal images, ten-day CGM traces and wrist-worn activity records is internally uneasy, even though the record correctly attributes the "No" answers to the healthsheet.

Licence scope tension. license_and_use_terms.license_terms grants use "for research, commercial and non-commercial purposes", while license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission is disease_specific_research and intended_uses.usage_notes states "The public version of the dataset may only be used for type 2 diabetes related research". The two are reconcilable only by reading the grant as permitting commercial T2DM research; the record does not say so.

regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is recorded as "restricted", which is more restrictive than either underlying source: the RO-Crate gives confidentialityLevel "HL7:2N (normal)" and the FAIRhub dataset description gives accessType "PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired". The record flags the mapping transparently in regulatory_restrictions.source_caveats, so this is a disclosed enum-mapping approximation rather than a hidden error, but a downstream consumer reading only the enum will overstate the access tier.

distribution_formats declares four formats (DICOM, CSV, JSON, Markdown) but does not list WFDB, which file_collections.cardiac_ecg records as the format of all 4,515 ECG files, and folds the .tsv metadata files (manifest.tsv, participants.tsv) under the CSV entry with media_type text/csv rather than text/tab-separated-values. The format inventory is therefore narrower and slightly less precise than the file_collections it summarises.

known_biases categorises selection_bias, sampling_bias and representation_bias but omits measurement or instrument bias, despite the record documenting six different retinal imaging device models across three sites, device-specific quality variation ("Optomed Aurora fundus photographs are taken undilated with a handheld camera, so image quality varies from patient to patient"), manual Spectralis operation, and three different blood-pressure device models. These are documented under anomalies and known_limitations but are not carried into the bias taxonomy, where a model developer would look for them.

future_use_impacts is absent. Social-impact material exists and is substantive — the addressing_gaps entry on the meta-epidemiological diversity finding, the known_biases mitigation strategies, the Native Biodata Consortium engagement, the community advisory board review of consent, and the scope_limitation noting that fairness analyses stratified by sex or race cannot be run on the public release — but it is scattered across five fields rather than gathered into the CROISSANT RAI social-impact slot that Q18 and Q20 read.

The institution accountable for the dataset is left unresolved across funders, creators, data_governance and license_and_use_terms: FAIRhub and the licence name Washington University in St. Louis (ROR 01yc7t268), while the RO-Crate places the PI in the Department of Ophthalmology at the University of Washington, NIH RePORTER lists the University of Washington as awardee, and the IRB is the University of Washington HSD. The record flags this in three places (creators.source_caveats, data_governance.source_caveats, top-level source_caveats) and declines to resolve it because both are tier 1. The disclosure is exemplary; the unresolved state still leaves a reader unable to name a single accountable steward.

Institutional attribution is internally discordant. The principal investigator Aaron Y. Lee is given the affiliation 'Washington University in St. Louis' with ROR:01yc7t268, and data_governance.accountable_organization repeats it, while every operational fact in the record points to the University of Washington: the IRB is University of Washington protocol STUDY00016228 with a uw.edu reliance contact and a Seattle postal address, NIH RePORTER records the awardee organization as University of Washington, the LeeLab Anura sensor was built at the University of Washington Karalis Johnson Retina Center, and central laboratory assays ran at the University of Washington Nutrition and Obesity Research Center. The record discloses the conflict in three source_caveats and resolves it by source tier rather than by plausibility, so the asserted accountable organization is likely an upstream FAIRhub conflation of two distinct institutions carried into the datasheet.

No software is named for any step that produced or transformed the distributed data. The release passed through substantial conversion — Topcon .fda and Heidelberg .sdt to DICOM, Philips XML to WFDB, Garmin .FIT to Open mHealth, REDCap exports to OMOP CDM tables, environmental readings to the NASA ASCII Earth-science format, plus static watermarking — and none of the seven preprocessing_strategies or three cleaning_strategies carries a used_software attachment or names a converter, pipeline or library. The software that is named occupies other roles: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application capture data, FAIRhub on Microsoft Azure hosts it, and the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard validates it. external_resources points at the GitHub organisation root https://github.com/AI-READI, which identifies the publisher rather than naming a tool.

The deidentification account holds two readings in tension. FAIRhub records deIdentType 'NoDeIdentification' with deIdentDirect true and deIdentHIPAA true, explaining that no identifiers were collected so none was necessary, while the Nature Metabolism comment describes the public set as stripped of PHI via the HIPAA Safe Harbor method — an active procedure. The record also notes that the healthsheet question on measures taken to avoid re-identification was left unanswered. The tension is explicitly surfaced in is_deidentified.source_caveats and the two readings agree on the outcome (no PHI in the public release), which substantially mitigates it.

No top-level download_url is populated. Platform access is nonetheless locatable: every distribution_formats entry carries access_urls https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access and data_governance.access_review_process states the three access steps.

Character encoding is not stated for any distribution. Formats are otherwise fully specified with media types, and the omission matters little for the binary DICOM, WFDB and .FIT-derived streams, but the CSV, TSV, JSON and Markdown members leave encoding unstated.

No governance committee contact person is asserted. data_governance.source_caveats states plainly that no source designates one; a committee_name (AI-READI Consortium) and general contacts (contact@aireadi.org, https://aireadi.org/contact, https://docs.aireadi.org/docs/3/contact) are given instead, and the Data Access Committee referenced for the controlled set is unnamed.

The variables block documents 26 representative measures in depth but carries no per-variable ontology or concept identifiers. Coded vocabularies are referenced only at the collection level (OMOP CDM one-to-one table mapping, RxNorm for medications), so a variable such as hba1c has no LOINC or OMOP concept ID attached, and the block covers a fraction of the full OMOP variable inventory.

Version 2.0.0 is recorded in version_access.version_details as no longer accessible, yet it is listed among versions_available with its DOI and appears in related_datasets as an is_new_version_of target. The claim is accurate rather than wrong, but a consumer resolving doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 from the relationship will not retrieve data.

data_protection_impacts records that no data protection impact analysis was conducted. This is a documented absence rather than a silent one, and a formal DPIA is not required of a US NIH study, but it leaves the element-4 assessment resting entirely on the IRB record.

Institutional attribution is internally implausible. The principal investigator Aaron Y. Lee is given the affiliation 'Washington University in St. Louis' with ROR:01yc7t268, and the same institution is named as accountable organization and licensor, while every other element of the record places the project at the University of Washington: IRB protocol STUDY00016228 of the 'University of Washington Institutional Review Board, Human Subjects Division' with the hsdrely@uw.edu contact and a Seattle postal address, the NIH RePORTER award organization 'University of Washington', the central laboratory 'University of Washington Nutrition and Obesity Research Center', and the LeeLab Anura sensor 'built ... at the Karalis Johnson Retina Center, University of Washington'. ROR 01yc7t268 denotes Washington University in St. Louis, a distinct institution from the University of Washington. The record discloses the tension in creators.source_caveats and data_governance.source_caveats and resolves it by source tier in favour of the less plausible reading.

De-identification claims conflict. is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present is false and is_deidentified.method states that 'no identifiers were collected so no active de-identification was necessary' (FAIRhub deIdentType 'NoDeIdentification'), while deidentification_details quotes the public set being 'stripped of Protected Health Information (PHI) ... via the Safe Harbor method', participant_privacy.anonymization_method describes 'Removal of HIPAA-defined Protected Health Information', and preprocessing_strategies lists 'Removal of protected health information, and of sex, race/ethnicity and medication information, from the public release'. A removal step either was or was not applied; the record also notes that the healthsheet question on measures to avoid re-identification was left unanswered.

A version that carries its own DOI is declared unavailable. version_access states 'Version 2.0.0 is recorded on FAIRhub and in its documentation as no longer accessible' while also listing 'version 2.0.0, DOI 10.60775/fairhub.2'. A resolvable persistent identifier whose object is withdrawn weakens the persistence claim on which Q13 and Q19 depend. The disclosed notice that 'This repository is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives' is a further, unquantified availability risk.

Sensitivity flags are more permissive than the surrounding controls. confidential_elements_present and sensitive_elements_present are both false and confidentiality_details asserts the dataset 'does not contain data that might be considered confidential', while the release is nevertheless governed by verified-ID login, a self-attestation access gate, per-licensee static watermarking, storage confined to institutional or BAA-covered infrastructure, and compliance with the NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy security standards, and participant_privacy acknowledges a theoretical re-identification risk.

No data protection impact analysis exists: data_protection_impacts records only that 'No data protection impact analysis has been conducted for the dataset'. This is an accurate disclosure, but it leaves the acknowledged re-identification risk unassessed for a human-subjects release, and it is the gap that keeps Q8 below the comprehensive band.

Two Q1 slots are unpopulated although equivalent content exists elsewhere: parent_datasets is absent (version predecessors are instead typed in related_datasets as is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and fairhub.1), and regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is unpopulated although the value 'HL7:2N (normal)' is recorded in regulatory_restrictions.notes. An errata slot is likewise absent, with changes carried in an external CHANGELOG.

at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included is false while special_protections enumerates substantive safeguards (age floor of 40 and ceiling of 85 excluding minors, exclusion of pregnancy, gestational diabetes and type 1 diabetes, capacity to consent, and an incidental-findings pathway for hypertensive crisis, retinal detachment, tumour and optic disc oedema). The flag and its content read in opposite directions, although the reading that no protected class is targeted is defensible.

subpopulations.source_caveats reports that the healthsheet answers 'No' to whether the dataset identifies demographic sub-populations, while four subpopulation objects with full distributions are serialized. The record reconciles this by noting that sex, race and ethnicity are withheld from the public release and that the counts come from the release README, but the serialized objects do not carry a per-object marker of which distributions are public and which are controlled-access aggregates.

ip_restrictions quotes the RO-Crate copyright notice 'Copyright (c) 2026 AI-READI' for a release issued 2025-11-17, a forward-dated notice relative to every other date in the record. Quoted faithfully from the source, but temporally anomalous.

No software is named for the transformations that produced the distributed data. preprocessing_strategies states in the passive voice that 'Topcon .fda and Heidelberg .sdt files are converted to DICOM, Garmin .FIT files are converted to the Open mHealth standard, and electrocardiogram data are stored in the WaveForm DataBase (WFDB) format', but names no converter, pipeline or version. Every tool the record does name occupies an excluded role: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application are capture, FAIRhub and Microsoft Azure are hosting, the RO-Crate/FAIRscape profile is metadata production, and the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard is validation of the released data rather than its production. The GitHub pointer identifies only the publisher organisation.

is_deidentified.method simultaneously reports that the FAIRhub dataset description records the de-identification type as 'NoDeIdentification' and that the public set is stripped of PHI 'using the Safe Harbor method', with identifiers_removed listing HIPAA PHI plus sex, race/ethnicity and medications. The two statements describe the same release and pull in opposite directions; the record flags the tension but leaves the structured method value carrying both readings.

variables is an explicitly partial inventory: eight substantive entries plus a 'Representative subset marker' entry stating that the complete variable documentation lives at https://docs.aireadi.org. No per-variable persistent identifiers (OMOP concept IDs, LOINC codes, column names) are given for any entry, so variable-level cross-dataset linking must be resolved outside the datasheet.

total_size_bytes (3,815,969,779,678) exceeds the sum of the nine datatype directory sizes (3,815,969,360,064) by 419,614 bytes. The record discloses the gap in source_caveats item (7) and states that the bundle does not explain it. The parallel file-count gap (356,343 total vs 356,334 across directories) is fully reconciled by the nine root-level metadata files, so only the byte discrepancy is unresolved.

Responsible-organisation conflict left unreconciled: data_governance.accountable_organization is Washington University in St. Louis (ROR:01yc7t268) and the licence names it as Licensor, while ethical_reviews and human_subject_research place IRB oversight, the reviewing body address and the reliance contact at the University of Washington. The RO-Crate label 'Washington University IRB' with a uw.edu contact compounds the ambiguity. The record discloses all of this in source_caveats items (2) and (3).

The planned longitudinal follow-up fraction is given as both 10% of the cohort (NIH RePORTER and the FAIRhub study description) and approximately 4% (healthsheet). The record records both rather than selecting, and correctly omits the figure from collection_timeframes rather than asserting one.

Two related_datasets entries use relationship_type 'is_described_by' with target_dataset pointing at journal-article DOIs (10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x, 10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449) rather than datasets. The record itself flags that these targets are articles, so the slot is being used deliberately to carry an attested relationship the schema has no better home for.

Two governance values are derived by the datasheet author rather than quoted from a source: confidentiality_level 'restricted' is inferred from the access model (the RO-Crate's own term is 'HL7:2N (normal)'), and hipaa_compliant 'compliant' is inferred from statements that no identifiers were collected and Safe Harbor was applied, with no source making a compliance determination in those words. Both derivations are disclosed in regulatory_restrictions.source_caveats and are reasonable, but they are judgements rather than attested facts.

No dedicated governance committee contact is recorded. data_governance carries committee_name, accountable_organization, access_review_process and stewardship_roles but no committee_contact; the reachable addresses are the study central contact (contact@aireadi.org) under maintainers and the IRB reliance mailbox (hsdrely@uw.edu) under human_subject_research. A prospective user with a governance question has no named committee contact.

No imputation_protocols slot is present. The substance is covered elsewhere: missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy states that missing values were filled only where directly derivable from other portions of an individual's record, under site PI approval, and otherwise left missing, with no instances excluded. This documents that statistical imputation was not used, but it is not discoverable from the imputation slot.

sensitive_elements carries two entries with directly contradictory booleans: the first sets sensitive_elements_present=false ('the public dataset does not contain data that is considered sensitive') and the second sets sensitive_elements_present=true, listing 'EHR, wearable monitoring, ECG, environmental sensor, continuous glucose monitor, and wearable accelerometer'. The record's prose explains that the two sources enumerate different things (sensitive attributes vs data-source categories) and nominates the healthsheet reading as governing, but a machine consumer reading the boolean slot receives an unresolved contradiction.

Responsible-institution conflict is recorded but left unresolved in the structured slots: data_governance.accountable_organization is 'Washington University in St. Louis' (ROR:01yc7t268) while human_subject_research.ethics_review_board and ethical_reviews[0].reviewing_organization name the 'University of Washington Human Subjects Division IRB' with a uw.edu reliance contact and a Seattle address, and the principal investigator's ORCID-bearing record is placed at the University of Washington by the RO-Crate. The two institutions are distinct legal entities; a reuser cannot tell which one holds accountability for the release.

data_protection_impacts is not populated even though the record documents processing of protected health information under HIPAA Safe Harbor, a controlled-access tier holding zip code, genetic sequencing data and medication history, and an explicit residual re-identification risk. The substance of an impact analysis is present (participant_privacy.reidentification_risk, future_use_impacts risk-and-mitigation statements, Level 3 data security classification), but no formal DPIA slot or document is referenced.

Recomputed arithmetic confirms the record's own disclosure: the nine datatype directory sizes sum to exactly 3,815,969,360,064 bytes, which is 419,614 bytes short of the reported total_size_bytes of 3,815,969,779,678. The shortfall is stated but unexplained, and the nine root-level metadata files that reconcile the file counts are far too small to account for 419 kB in aggregate only if they are unusually large, so the residual is plausible but unattributed.

is_deidentified records internally tense claims: identifiable_elements_present=false with the reasoning that 'no identifiers were collected, so no active de-identification was necessary' and FAIRhub's de-identification type recorded as 'NoDeIdentification', while the same field asserts that the public set is 'stripped of Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule using the Safe Harbor method' and that direct identifier removal and HIPAA de-identification are flagged as applied. Safe Harbor is an affirmative de-identification procedure; 'NoDeIdentification' and 'Safe Harbor applied' cannot both be literally true.

regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level='restricted' and regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant='compliant' are both derived rather than quoted, as the record itself discloses; the only confidentiality term in the sources is the RO-Crate's 'HL7:2N (normal)', which is a materially less restrictive characterization, and no source makes a HIPAA compliance determination in those words.

The planned Year-4 longitudinal follow-up fraction is reported as both 10% (NIH RePORTER, FAIRhub study description) and approximately 4% (healthsheet) and is left unresolved in relationships.source_caveats and collection_timeframes.source_caveats. Both sources are tier-1 by the record's own ranking, so no value is stated.

Three named schema slots that this rubric reads are empty although adjacent content partly supplies their substance: discouraged_uses (no equivalent content anywhere; prohibited_uses covers prohibitions, not discouraged practices), errata (the CHANGELOG is referenced but no erratum slot exists), and was_derived_from / parent_datasets (version lineage is carried instead by related_datasets typed relationships is_new_version_of to fairhub.2 and fairhub.1).

The stated recommended split proportion of '70%/15%/15%' does not exactly match the stated split sizes: 1,576/352/352 of 2,280 is 69.1%/15.4%/15.4%. The deviation is small and is the expected consequence of forcing exactly 88 participants per race/ethnicity cell in the validation and test sets, but the nominal proportion is presented as if exact.

Keyword coverage is adequate in count (9) but under-represents modalities that dominate the release by volume and by scientific distinctiveness: there is no keyword for optical coherence tomography or OCT angiography (together 230,199 files, the large majority of the release), none for fluorescence lifetime imaging ophthalmoscopy, none for wearable/accelerometry, none for environmental or indoor air-quality sensing, and none for OMOP CDM. 'Eye exam' is a low-specificity stand-in for four distinct ophthalmic imaging modalities.

sensitive_elements_present: false and confidential_elements_present: false sit uneasily with regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted, HIPAA-oriented handling, static watermarking of released copies, verified-ID access gating and an acknowledged theoretical re-identification risk. A release that genuinely contains nothing sensitive or confidential would not normally require that control stack; the two blocks appear to answer the healthsheet's narrow questions rather than characterise the release as governed.

is_deidentified carries three mutually inconsistent source statements: FAIRhub records 'NoDeIdentification' (no identifiers collected), the RO-Crate records the release as deidentified, and the Nature Metabolism comment describes HIPAA Safe Harbor stripping. The structured method field asserts the strongest of the three (HIPAA Safe Harbor) while deidentification_details reports all three unreconciled.

No download_url field is populated. The download route is nevertheless reconstructable from page, data_governance.access_review_process (verified-ID login, T2DM-only attestation, license assent) and the external resource https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access, so the sub-element's purpose is met by platform access instructions rather than by a direct link.

distribution_formats lists DICOM, CSV, JSON and Markdown, but the release also distributes WFDB electrocardiography records, Open mHealth wearable/CGM payloads and NASA ESDS-style ASCII environmental files per conforms_to and file_collections. The distribution list is narrower than the standards list, and no character encoding is stated anywhere.

is_tabular: false while the description states the modalities 'encompass tabular data, imaging data and physiological signal/waveform data' and clinical_data is distributed as one-to-one OMOP CDM CSV tables. The flag is defensible for a multimodal release that is not a single table, but read alone it contradicts the description.

No software that produced or transformed the released data is named. Conversion of Topcon .fda and FLIO .sdt exports to DICOM, of Garmin .FIT to Open mHealth, and mapping of clinical data to OMOP CDM are described as having happened, but no tool, package, version or repository is attached to any of those steps, and no used_software is recorded on preprocessing_strategies or cleaning_strategies. The software that is named occupies non-qualifying roles: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application are capture instrumentation; FAIRhub on Microsoft Azure is hosting; the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard is validation of the released data; https://github.com/AI-READI is an organisation root that identifies the publisher rather than a piece of software.

variables provides 20 measures with name, data type, unit, description and measurement technique, but no ontology or concept identifiers (LOINC, OMOP concept_id, SNOMED) are attached, and source_caveats records that the authoritative per-domain data dictionary at docs.aireadi.org was not consulted. Variable coverage is therefore illustrative rather than exhaustive for a 356,343-file multimodal release.

No errata block and no data_protection_impacts (DPIA) block. Change information is instead carried by updates.update_details and version_access.version_details, and data-protection reasoning by participant_privacy and ethical_reviews, so both sub-elements are satisfied through their alternative fields rather than left undocumented.

Institutional attribution is internally contradictory across the record: Washington University in St. Louis is named as licensor, accountable organization and PI affiliation, while the reviewing IRB, the award recipient per NIH RePORTER and the assay laboratory are all University of Washington. The record discloses the conflict in source_caveats rather than resolving it, which is honest but leaves accountable_organization pointing at an institution that no human-subjects or award evidence supports.

Collection start is given as 2023-07-19 in collection_timeframes and the description while the BMJ Open protocol states 18 July 2023; license naming differs between two tier-1 sources ('AI-READI custom license v2.0' in the API, 'Health Data License' on the dataset page); a healthsheet answer describing first-year coverage contradicts the stated 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01 window. All three are disclosed and adjudicated by source tier rather than left silent.

sensitive_elements_present=false and confidential_elements_present=false are asserted for a release comprising retinal imaging (DICOM), continuous glucose traces, wrist-worn biometric signals (heart rate, SpO2, sleep, stress) and in-home environmental sensing. These declarations contradict the same record's restricted confidentiality_level, its verified-ID plus license-assent access gate, its static watermarking of released copies, and participant_privacy.reidentification_risk, which concedes a theoretical future re-identification risk from AI inference. A dataset that needs watermarking and a DUA to protect subjects is not plausibly free of sensitive elements, even post-Safe-Harbor.

Institutional attribution is internally divergent in the structured fields, not only in prose. creators.affiliations[0] and data_governance.accountable_organization both assert Washington University in St. Louis (ROR:01yc7t268) as the accountable organization and PI affiliation, while ethical_reviews.reviewing_organization and human_subject_research.ethics_review_board assert the University of Washington IRB with a UW Human Subjects Division address, and NIH RePORTER is reported as recording award OT2OD032644 to the University of Washington. A consumer reading only the machine-readable fields obtains an institutional attribution that the record's own source_caveats says is contested.

is_deidentified carries two mutually exclusive claims in one object: identifiable_elements_present=false with method 'HIPAA Safe Harbor' and identifiers_removed listing PHI, alongside deidentification_details reporting FAIRhub's de-identification type of 'NoDeIdentification' on the ground that no identifiers were ever collected. 'Safe Harbor stripping was performed' and 'no de-identification was necessary' cannot both describe the same processing step.

future_use_impacts states the creators 'do not currently anticipate uses of the dataset that could result in unfair treatment of individuals or groups', while known_biases documents representation_bias (no Pacific Islanders or Native Americans), sampling_bias (urban, hospital-based recruitment) and English-language selection bias, and known_limitations states that models 'may not generalize to populations, settings or cultural and socioeconomic backgrounds that the three recruiting health systems do not reach'. The limitations section anticipates precisely the differential model performance the impact statement declines to anticipate.

Stated totals do not reconcile with the enumerated collections. total_file_count is 356,343 while the nine data-type directory counts sum to 356,334, and total_size_bytes is 3,815,969,779,678 while directory sizes sum to 3,815,969,360,064 (a 419,614-byte shortfall). The record identifies both gaps and separately states that the structure description lists exactly nine root-level metadata files, which accounts for the nine-file difference precisely, yet it presents the discrepancy as unreconciled.

data_protection_impacts is absent. For a DUA-gated multimodal health release that explicitly contemplates AI-driven re-identification and applies watermarking as a countermeasure, a data protection impact assessment is the field that would record that reasoning. Its absence is the principal gap keeping Q8 below the comprehensive band.

Provenance is documented substantively in prose but not in the fields that carry it. was_derived_from, parent_datasets and errata are all empty, so the derivation chain (device-native .xml/.csv/.fda/.sdt/.FIT exports, conversion to DICOM and Open mHealth, OMOP CDM mapping, site QC, central processing, FAIRhub upload) must be reassembled by the reader from raw_data_sources, preprocessing_strategies, data_collectors and related_datasets.

Preprocessing and conversion are described as operations without naming the software that performs them. The .fda and .sdt to DICOM converters, the .FIT to Open mHealth converter and the OMOP mapping pipeline are all described by effect, with no tool names, versions or repository paths, even though external_resources links the project's GitHub organization. labeling_strategies, machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses and imputation_protocols are empty, though the record justifies each absence (hypothesis-agnostic, unlabelled, no imputation of missing modalities).

Version persistence is compromised in a way the record discloses: version_access marks version 2.0.0 as 'no longer accessible' although it holds a minted DOI (10.60775/fairhub.2), and notes records that the repository 'is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives'. Both bear directly on the long-term sustainability claim underlying Q13.

sampling_strategies sets is_sample=false, is_random=false and is_representative=false while the strategies text describes non-probability wave-based sampling of a health-system population with deliberate under- and oversampling. The record notes the healthsheet answers 'N/A' to the sampling question while the study is itself a non-probability sample, so the boolean and the prose encode different answers.

The variables list enumerates 20 measures drawn, as source_caveats concedes, from the protocol publication and healthsheet device descriptions rather than the released data dictionary. For a 356,343-file release spanning OMOP clinical tables, laboratory panels, imaging and waveform modalities, this is illustrative rather than complete; the authoritative per-domain documentation at docs.aireadi.org was outside the input bundle.

ip_restrictions records the copyright notice 'Copyright (c) 2026 AI-READI' while issued and the version 3.0.0 release date are both 2025-11-17. The copyright year postdates the stated publication date of the version being described.

keywords contains 7 terms, one short of the diversity threshold, and omits several prominent modalities that the description and file_collections treat as first-class (OCT angiography, fluorescence lifetime imaging ophthalmoscopy, wearable activity monitoring, environmental sensing, OMOP).

discouraged_uses is empty. The record draws a sharp permitted/prohibited boundary through six detailed prohibited_uses but records no middle tier, although the documented biases imply uses that are permitted yet inadvisable, such as training deployment models for populations the three sites do not reach.

A healthsheet answer quoted in source_caveats states the dataset 'contains data from all participants who have been enrolled during the first year of data collection', which conflicts with the same document's July 19, 2023 to May 1, 2025 coverage and with the 2280-participant count of version 3.0.0. The record identifies the contradiction as a source defect rather than propagating it into the structured fields.

No software that produced or transformed the distributed data is named. preprocessing_strategies states that Topcon .fda and Heidelberg .sdt exports were 'converted to DICOM', Garmin .FIT 'converted to the Open mHealth standard', ECG 'converted to WFDB', and that clinical data were 'mapped to' the OMOP CDM, but no converter, mapper or pipeline is identified; processing is described only as 'a combination of automated and custom processing'. The named software in the record occupies non-qualifying roles: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application are capture, FAIRhub on Microsoft Azure is hosting, the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard is validation, and https://github.com/AI-READI is an organization root that identifies the publisher rather than a tool.

No download_url slot is populated even though the release is publicly downloadable. Access is nevertheless actionable from other slots: distribution_formats.access_urls gives https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access and data_governance.access_review_process records the FAIRhub access type 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired' and the three steps required.

The de-identification evidence carries an internal tension the record itself surfaces: is_deidentified.deidentification_details reports the FAIRhub deIdentType as 'NoDeIdentification' with deIdentHIPAA true, while is_deidentified.method asserts the public set is stripped of PHI 'via the Safe Harbor method'. The record reconciles this by explaining that no identifiers were collected so no active de-identification step was necessary, which is a coherent reading, but the two statements read as contradictory in isolation.

total_size_bytes is stated as 3,815,969,779,678 while the nine file_collections directory sizes sum to 3,815,969,360,064, a difference of 419,614 bytes that no source accounts for. The record discloses this discrepancy in source_caveats and attributes it plausibly to the root-level metadata files.

regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted' and hipaa_compliant 'compliant' are the record's own mappings onto the schema vocabulary, not values any source states; the only source value is the RO-Crate's 'HL7:2N (normal)'. The record declares this inference in source_caveats rather than presenting the enum values as sourced, which is the correct handling, but a consumer reading only the structured slot would not see the inference.

variables documents 13 variables (participant_id, seven laboratory analytes, MoCA, visual acuity, contrast sensitivity, CGM, particulate matter) for a release whose clinical_data directory is a one-to-one mapping of OMOP CDM tables covering surveys, assessments and laboratory results. Variable-level coverage is therefore illustrative rather than exhaustive, though the entries present carry data_type, unit, measurement_technique, reference ranges and an is_identifier flag.

data_governance records committee_name, accountable_organization, access_review_process and stewardship_roles but no committee_contact. A contact is reachable elsewhere (maintainers gives contact@aireadi.org and https://aireadi.org/contact; human_subject_research.ethics_review_board gives hsdrely@uw.edu for the IRB Reliance Team), so the governance-contact requirement is met in substance but not in the dedicated slot.

Three named evidence slots are empty where their subject matter is nevertheless addressed in prose: errata (change information is instead in updates.update_details and version_access.version_details), imputation_protocols (missing-value handling is in missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy), and data_protection_impacts (the notes field states that no data protection impact analysis has been conducted).

is_deidentified is internally contradictory. method states 'No active de-identification was necessary because no identifiers were collected' and simultaneously that 'The public set is stripped of Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule via the Safe Harbor method'. deidentification_details then records the FAIRhub value deIdentType 'NoDeIdentification' alongside deIdentHIPAA true and deIdentDirect true. 'No de-identification was necessary', 'Safe Harbor stripping was performed' and 'NoDeIdentification' cannot all describe the same processing step; identifiers_removed further lists four categories actively removed (PHI, sex, race/ethnicity, medications), which is an active removal, not an absence of need.

Confidentiality and sensitivity declarations conflict with the governance controls actually imposed. confidential_elements_present is false and sensitive_elements_present is false, yet regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is 'restricted', the license prohibits re-identification and contact with data subjects, mandates storage only on institutional servers or HIPAA-BAA-covered cloud, permits static watermarking to identify the licensee, and access requires verified-ID login plus self-attestation. A release with no confidential and no sensitive elements would not require this control set.

version_access.versions_available enumerates versions 1.0.0 and 2.0.0 with their DOIs as available, while version_details in the same block states that both 'are no longer accessible through FAIRhub'. Two minted DOIs (10.60775/fairhub.1 and 10.60775/fairhub.2) therefore no longer resolve to retrievable data, which contradicts the persistent-identifier premise underlying the record's FAIR and sustainability claims.

No data protection impact assessment exists and the structured slot is empty, yet the record acknowledges a theoretical re-identification risk driven by AI inference and asserts regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant: 'compliant'. The negative finding ('no data protection impact analysis has been conducted') is disclosed only in free-text notes, not in data_protection_impacts, so the gap is not machine-discoverable. A DPIA is the expected artifact precisely where an acknowledged re-identification pathway meets a broad reuse licence.

Unresolved institutional attribution across two distinct ROR identities. ROR:01yc7t268 is Washington University in St. Louis and ROR:00cvxb145 is the University of Washington; the record assigns the former as managing organization, lead sponsor, licensor, governance accountable_organization and PI affiliation, and the latter as the PI's department and the IRB's actual address (hsdrely@uw.edu, Human Subjects Division, Seattle). The IRB label 'Washington University IRB' with a University of Washington address and contact is an internal contradiction in the source that propagates into ethical_reviews and data_governance.accountable_organization, leaving legal accountability for the licence and the IRB of record ambiguous.

Size arithmetic does not close. The nine datatype directory totals sum to 3,815,969,360,064 bytes against a stated total_size_bytes of 3,815,969,779,678, a 419,614-byte shortfall. The record discloses the difference and offers root-level metadata files as a plausible but unverified explanation. By contrast the file-count arithmetic does close exactly (356,334 + 9 root files = 356,343), which makes the unexplained byte gap the weaker of the two reconciliations.

Sampling characterization conflicts across same-tier sources: the healthsheet answers that the dataset 'contains all possible instances' and returns 'N/A' for sampling strategy, while the FAIRhub study description registers samplingMethod 'Non-Probability Sample' and the protocol describes wave-based, EHR-screened, balance-adjusted contact pools. The record sets is_sample: true and reasons the conflict out in source_caveats, which is the defensible resolution but remains an unreconciled source disagreement.

Version scope conflict: the healthsheet and RO-Crate describe version 3.0.0 as covering data 'up through the end of the second year of the study', while the README changelog attributes 863 participants to year 2 and 1,213 to year 3. Separately the v3.0.0 documentation 'About' page reuses v2.0.0 wording describing a version containing 'data from the participants of the pilot study phase', which is inconsistent with 2,280 participants over 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01.

No errata slot is populated across three releases, although a substantive corrective change is documented: the Snellen visual-acuity variables were dropped between 2.0.0 and 3.0.0, leaving only logMAR. A dropped variable is errata-adjacent and is currently discoverable only from version_details prose.

The licence is named three different ways: the top-level license field says 'AI-READI custom license v2.0', license_and_use_terms resolves it to https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036 (valid Zenodo prefix), and the notes record that FAIRhub pages label it 'Health Data License'. A consumer matching on the licence string will not match across platforms.

Device heterogeneity is not categorized as a bias. Retinal imaging was acquired on four OCT/OCTA vendor platforms (Heidelberg Spectralis, Topcon Maestro2, Topcon Triton, Zeiss Cirrus) and four fundus platforms, and the record notes that Optomed Aurora image quality 'varies from patient to patient and within the same patient'. Cross-device systematic difference is a textbook measurement_bias for multimodal imaging AI, but it appears only under anomalies, so known_biases omits a bias type that the dataset's own acquisition design makes likely.

Two NIH RePORTER project-detail identifiers (10885481 and 10471118) are cited for the same core award OT2OD032644, and the healthsheet transcribes the award number as 'OT2ODO32644', substituting the letter O for a zero. Both defects are disclosed by the record and the canonical award number is carried correctly in the structured grant_number slot.

at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included is false while special_protections is populated with substantive protections. The protections are in fact exclusion criteria (no minors, prisoners, pregnant women or adults unable to consent), so the flag and the list are describing opposite things under one heading.

Element 8 sub-element 4: the record describes format conversion and processing of the released data (.fda and .sdt to DICOM, Garmin .FIT to Open mHealth, 'a combination of automated and custom processing') but never names the software that performed any of it. Every piece of software named in the record occupies an excluded role: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application are capture and data-entry tools (role a); FAIRhub is the hosting and dissemination platform (role b); the RO-Crate packaging wraps the release without transforming its contents (role c); the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard, supported by the included dqd_omop.json, is a validation aid for downstream users (role d). The GitHub pointer is an organization root (https://github.com/AI-READI) that identifies the publisher rather than a named conversion or processing tool.

regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is set to 'restricted', a value the record itself states is its own substitution that 'does not reproduce, and on its face contradicts' the only sourced classification, the RO-Crate's HL7:2N (normal). It also sits against confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present: false. The substitution is disclosed rather than concealed, which is good practice, but the asserted enum value is not supported by any source.

Three incompatible characterizations of deidentification are carried simultaneously: is_deidentified.method reports FAIRhub's 'NoDeIdentification' with identifiable_elements_present: false (no identifiers collected into the release), the RO-Crate records deidentified: true, and the Nature Metabolism comment describes HIPAA Safe Harbor stripping of Protected Health Information. Safe Harbor stripping and 'no de-identification was necessary' are different operational claims about the same release. The record documents the disagreement in source_caveats rather than resolving it.

sensitive_elements.sensitive_elements_present is true, enumerating EHR, wearable, ECG, environmental and CGM categories from the RO-Crate, while the FAIRhub healthsheet position recorded in the same block asserts the public dataset contains no sensitive data, and confidential_elements_present is false. Both tier-1 positions are retained without adjudication.

sampling_strategies.is_sample is false while the same block documents non-probability, wave-based stratified recruitment from an EHR-derived study base with deliberate under- and oversampling. The record scopes is_sample to enrollment completeness and warns the reader, but the boolean read alone contradicts the prose.

No download_url slot is populated. Access is nonetheless fully actionable: page gives https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 and data_governance.access_review_process publishes the access route at https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access together with the exact conditions (verified ID login, type-2-diabetes-research attestation, license acceptance, access type PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired).

No errata slot is populated. Change documentation is carried by updates.update_details pointing at the CHANGELOG, by the version_access note that 2.0.0 is no longer accessible, and by the known_limitations entry recording that Snellen visual acuity variables were dropped in 3.0.0; no corrections to previously released values are reported as such.

instances.data_topic carries the bare CURIE B2AI_TOPIC:43 with no label or resolvable URI, so the coded topic is not machine- or human-resolvable from the record alone. The condition coverage is recoverable from description, subpopulations and known_limitations (type 2 diabetes across four severity arms), which is why the sub-element still passes.

Unresolved institutional attribution: the acronym expansion ('Exploratory' versus 'Equitable'), the lead institution (Washington University in St. Louis as FAIRhub managing organization and license Licensor versus University of Washington as RO-Crate PI affiliation and NIH RePORTER awardee) and the publisher (FAIRhub versus AI-READI Consortium) each differ between equally ranked sources. The record carries both positions in source_caveats rather than asserting one silently, which is the correct handling, but a consumer of creators.principal_investigator.affiliation receives two affiliations for one person.

The RO-Crate copyright notice quoted in ip_restrictions reads 'Copyright (c) 2026 AI-READI' for a release issued 2025-11-17. The value is faithfully quoted from the source, so this is a source artifact rather than a record error, but it is temporally inconsistent with issued and distribution_dates.

The confidentiality and sensitivity fields do not compose into one coherent statement. regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is 'restricted', while confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present is false and is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present is false, and sensitive_elements_present is true. A machine consumer reading the enum alone would classify the release as restricted-confidential, which the confidential_elements object denies.

regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted is, by the record's own notes, a substitution that 'does not reproduce, and on its face contradicts' the only value any declared source states (the RO-Crate's 'HL7:2N (normal)'). The asserted enum value is therefore not source-backed, even though the substitution is disclosed and reasoned.

The de-identification method is left under-determined across three conflicting characterizations that the record carries without resolution: FAIRhub 'NoDeIdentification' (no identifiers collected into the release), RO-Crate 'deidentified: true', and Nature Metabolism 'HIPAA Safe Harbor stripping'. The University of Washington IRB protocol separately shows that direct identifiers (name, MRN, DOB, address, phone, email, driver's licence) were collected and code-linked in the study. A reuser assessing re-identification risk cannot tell from this record which method actually governs the released files.

sampling_strategies.is_sample is false while the same object's strategies field describes non-probability, wave-based stratified recruitment from an EHR-derived study base, and is_representative is false with a why_not_representative narrative. The record flags the tension itself and scopes is_sample to enrollment completeness, but the boolean as serialized contradicts the prose beside it.

Institutional attribution is internally divided: Washington University in St. Louis (ROR:01yc7t268) is recorded as accountable organization, managing organization and Licensor, while the IRB (STUDY00016228), the Human Subjects Division, the assay laboratory (UW Nutrition and Obesity Research Center) and the custom environmental sensor lab (Karalis Johnson Retina Center) are all University of Washington. The ROR identifier does match the name it is attached to, so this is a source conflict rather than a malformed identifier, but the governance chain as asserted places accountability at an institution that performs none of the documented oversight functions.

Several rubric-referenced fields have no slot in the record even where the substance exists in prose: no download_url (access URL appears only inside data_governance.access_review_process), no errata (the CHANGELOG is referenced but not enumerated), no was_derived_from or parent_datasets (version lineage is expressed only through related_datasets), no resources, no labeling_strategies (addressed as an explicit negative in instances.label_description) and no imputation_protocols (addressed in missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy).

data_protection_impacts records that no DPIA was conducted, while the same record documents human subject research on health data, an acknowledged theoretical re-identification risk, and a companion controlled-access release holding ZIP code, race, sex and genetic data. The negative is reported honestly as an explicit answer rather than an omission, but it is a substantive protection gap rather than a documentation gap.

The reuse permission is stated at two different scopes without reconciliation: license_and_use_terms.license_terms grants use 'for research, commercial and non-commercial purposes', while data_use_permission is disease_specific_research and intended_uses records the access condition limiting the public release to type 2 diabetes related research. The record discloses the divergence, but the enum and the license text would license different downstream uses if read independently.

Grant number OT2OD032644 is recorded in the canonical core-project form while the RO-Crate cites 1OT2OD032644 and two declared sources link the same core project to different RePORTER records (10885481 and 10471118). The core number itself is well-formed NIH and the divergence is disclosed; the effect is cosmetic.

Two facts reported in the record undercut the persistence its sustainability documentation otherwise establishes: version 2.0.0 carries its own DOI (10.60775/fairhub.2) yet is recorded as 'no longer accessible', and both FAIRhub and the documentation site carry the notice that the repository 'is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives'. The documentation of these facts is exemplary; the facts themselves are adverse to DOI persistence and long-term availability.

human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects=true and the cohort is described as critically ill hospital patients including PICU and NICU admissions, but no IRB, ethics committee, or approval identifier is recorded anywhere. The two ethical_reviews entries name 'CHoRUS consortium' as reviewing_organization and describe community ethics focus groups and legal-landscape analysis, which is consortium ethics activity rather than a formal review of the dataset; the record's own source_caveats concede this.

involves_human_subjects=true but informed_consent is entirely absent. For a retrospective EHR extraction a waiver of consent or an exemption determination is the expected documentation, and neither is present, so a reuser cannot tell on what legal basis patient data were assembled.

is_deidentified is populated with a plausible method, and sensitive_elements declares protected health information across nine modalities from US hospitals, yet regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant is absent, regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance is absent, and no data_protection_impacts entry exists. Deidentification is claimed without naming a standard (no Safe Harbor or Expert Determination reference).

No DOI is present for the dataset. The identifier supplied, id: https://chorus4ai.org/#dataset, is a fragment URI on a project marketing site, not a persistent identifier; publisher is also absent, so neither a registrar nor a hosting repository can be resolved. The record's top-level source_caveats confirms the bundle gives no DOI.

One external resource, 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus', is recorded without a URL scheme and is therefore not a resolvable URI as written. The record flags that it is reproduced as published, but the value remains machine-unresolvable.

collection_timeframes reports 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30, which is the NIH award period for OT2OD032701 rather than the clinical period the admissions are drawn from. Because acquisition_methods describe retrospective extraction, the admissions largely predate the award, so the stated timeframe is semantically the wrong interval for the data. The record itself identifies this substitution.

Two sources quantify the dataset differently: 50,000 admissions and 7,642 admissions with radiology data (project website) versus 'over 45K unique admissions' and 1000 images (August 2025 webinar). instances.counts asserts the tier-2 figures as the values of record. The disclosure is exemplary, but the asserted counts remain unreconciled and the imaging figures are in incompatible units.

conforms_to_standard collapses EDF+, Persyst, and the OHNLP open source schema into a single OTHER token, and lists WFDB for what the narrative describes as an extended PhysioNet schema. The machine-readable conformance list therefore understates and slightly misstates the standards actually in use relative to the conforms_to prose, weakening the interoperability signal it exists to carry.

status is 'partially released' and updates describes modalities still in flux (imaging deidentification and EEG extraction in process as of August 2025), yet version, version_access, errata, and any release date are all absent. A reuser who receives an extract cannot identify which state of a moving dataset they hold, which undermines the reproducibility of any analysis built on it.

known_biases records one entry whose bias_description states that the project 'treats cohort balance and diversity as an open risk to be managed' and cites the aspiration to build the most diverse dataset. That is an intention and a mitigation posture, not a characterized bias of the released data. No fairness analysis or demographic distribution is given even though demographics and social determinants of health are collected modalities, and obvious candidates (selection bias from 14 academic centers, measurement bias across heterogeneous site documentation practices) are not categorized.

The maintainer contact email domain is recorded as 'mgh.havard.edu' (misspelling of harvard), reproduced verbatim from the source with a caveat. The contact is transparently sourced but not actionable as written.

license_and_use_terms establishes controlled access conditional on a signed licensing agreement, but no license document, DUA template, or agreement identifier is referenced, and no download_url or enclave access endpoint is given. The prohibition-side terms that a signed agreement would carry are also absent from prohibited_uses and discouraged_uses.

human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects=true for a multicenter dataset of 50,000 ICU/PICU/NICU admissions, but no IRB approval, ethics board of record, or data protection impact assessment is documented. The record's own source_caveats state 'The bundle does not state IRB approval for the dataset or name an ethics review board of record.' The ethical_reviews entries describe community ethics focus groups and legal-landscape research by consortium pillars, which is ethics activity rather than review or approval of this data collection.

involves_human_subjects=true but informed_consent is entirely absent. For retrospective EHR/waveform/imaging extraction a consent waiver is the expected documentation, and neither consent nor waiver is recorded.

is_deidentified.method claims tokenization and 'transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification', and sensitive_elements flags patient-level clinical data including waveforms, imaging, notes and social determinants of health, yet participant_privacy and an explicit re-identification risk assessment are absent. High-resolution waveform and imaging data carry known re-identification risk that is never assessed.

The deidentification method is described procedurally (tokenization, CTP-deid, privacy_scan_tool, imaging de-id in process) but no recognized standard is named (HIPAA Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, k-anonymity), and no HIPAA compliance status is recorded anywhere despite US hospital PHI being the source.

No persistent identifier: doi is absent and id is the project homepage https://chorus4ai.org/, which is a web address rather than a DOI, RRID, ARK or Handle. Correspondingly no citation and no publisher are recorded, so the dataset cannot be cited or cross-referenced.

No variable-level metadata at all: variables is absent, is_tabular is unset, and no data dictionary is referenced, despite 1.6 billion rows of OMOP-standardized tabular data. OMOP conformance implies a known column vocabulary but does not document the extensions the record itself claims for nursing flowsheets.

license_and_use_terms documents only the AIM-AHEAD training-programme licensing agreement and explicitly notes that no general license for the data is stated; there are also no prohibited_uses or discouraged_uses for a sensitive clinical corpus.
