prohibited_uses and discouraged_uses are both absent for a controlled-access dataset of critically ill patients' PHI. intended_uses is developed in detail across three categories, so the use guidance is one-sided: no prohibition on re-identification attempts, redistribution, or clinical deployment of unvalidated models is recorded, even though such terms are presumably in the signed licensing agreement.

No version identifier, version_access or errata exist for a dataset that is explicitly and actively growing (updates describes expansion toward 100,000 admissions across 9 modalities, with imaging and EEG still arriving). Users cannot name which state of a moving dataset they analysed, and the maintainers entry notes a package status page listing versions for software while the dataset itself carries none.

No common identifier for cross-modality linkage is documented. The datasheet describes nine modality subsets held in different places (OMOP and telemetry in the enclave, notes local to sites, imaging and EEG partly pending) but never states the key on which an admission's OMOP rows, waveforms, images and note tokens are joined — the central integration question for a multimodal AI-ready dataset.

The external resource 'CHoRUS page on the Bridge2AI website' is recorded as 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus' without a URI scheme, unlike the other two external resources which are well-formed https URIs. As written it is not a resolvable URI value.

The maintainer contact address 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu' contains a misspelled domain ('havard' for 'harvard'). The record transcribes the published value faithfully and flags the error in source_caveats, which is the right provenance behaviour, but the listed maintainer contact is not usable as given.

collection_timeframes is populated but gives no clinical date range: it states retrospective collection reflecting a state 'as of August 2025' without the admission years covered. A critical care cohort whose temporal span is unknown cannot be assessed for practice drift, COVID-era effects, or comparability with other ICU datasets.

sampling_strategies.is_sample=true and describes an intent to ensure a balanced, diverse cohort, but its own source_caveats concedes that the executed sampling frame, inclusion criteria and any verification of representativeness are undocumented. Stated intent is therefore not evidence of the released cohort's composition, and the same gap weakens the selection-bias mitigation claim in known_biases.

human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is true and the dataset comprises hospital records of critically ill patients, but no informed_consent field is present and no waiver of consent is recorded. direct_collection.is_direct=false establishes that collection was retrospective, which is a plausible basis for a consent waiver, but the record never states that a waiver was granted or by whom.

human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is true, yet ethical_reviews records only community-facing ethics focus groups and perspective-gathering. No institutional review board, ethics committee, reviewing organization or approval number is named for the dataset, and data_protection_impacts is absent. The record's own source_caveats state this gap explicitly.

is_deidentified describes tokenization and imaging de-identification but names no de-identification standard (HIPAA Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, k-anonymity), enumerates no identifiers removed, and reports no residual re-identification risk. participant_privacy is populated with protections but carries no reidentification_risk assessment, and data_protection_impacts is absent. For 1.6 billion rows of timestamped ICU EHR data plus waveforms and imaging, the method applied to the structured OMOP data is never stated.

at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included is true and PICU/NICU admissions place minors and neonates in the released data, but no assent procedures, guardian consent procedures, or special protections are documented, and participant_compensation is absent (plausibly not applicable for retrospective data but not stated as such).

No DOI is present for a dataset described as released. The id field is https://chorus4ai.org/, the project homepage, which is byte-identical to the page field. A homepage URL that doubles as the landing page is not a distinct, persistent, dataset-level identifier and will not resolve to a specific release.

Two volume disagreements are retained rather than reconciled: the project website reports 50,000 released admissions while the September 2025 webinar reports over 45,000 unique admissions as of August 2025; and the website reports 7,642 admissions with radiology data while the webinar reports roughly 1,000 images available with de-identification in process. The record discloses both disagreements and its ranking rule, which is good provenance practice, but a reuser cannot determine the volume of the release they would receive.

instances.counts of 1600000000 is disclosed by the record as its own expansion of the rounded website figure '1.6 Billion Rows', not a count reported exactly by any source. The disclosure is appropriate, but the integer reads as more precise than its provenance supports.

regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is 'restricted' and the data are US hospital records subject to HIPAA, but no HIPAA, GDPR or export-control determination is recorded. HIPAA and GDPR appear in the record only as topics of a training workshop, which is not a compliance determination for the dataset.

The dataset is described as partially released and actively expanding toward 100,000 admissions, but version, version_access and errata are all absent and updates.source_caveats confirms no versioning policy is stated. A user cannot cite, reproduce against, or diff a specific release.

license_and_use_terms notes an MIT/Apache-2.0 license that the record correctly attributes to the chorus-ai software repositories rather than the clinical dataset, but no data use license is named for a dataset that third_party_sharing.is_shared marks as shared. The licensing agreement is referenced only through the AIM-AHEAD training-program registration flow and is not reproduced.

The maintainer contact email 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu' contains an apparent misspelling of the domain ('havard'). The record flags it as 'address as printed on the site', so the error is faithfully carried rather than introduced, but the address as recorded is not deliverable.

notes reproduces a site-wide banner stating the repository is 'under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives' (including the upstream typo 'repoitory'). This is a material availability signal for a prospective reuser, but the record does not state what, if anything, it implies for current access or content.

human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects=true for a 50,000-admission clinical EHR dataset, but ethical_reviews names no institutional review board, ethics committee or reviewing organization and states no approval number. The two ethical_reviews entries describe community ethics focus groups and community-perspective research, which are project ethics activities rather than regulatory review of the dataset. The record itself discloses this gap in human_subject_research.source_caveats ('The bundle does not name an IRB or ethics review board, nor state an approval number, for the dataset.'), which is honest but does not supply the missing governance evidence.

involves_human_subjects=true but there is no informed_consent field at all. For a retrospective EHR/PACS/telemetry dataset the expected documentation is a waiver of informed consent or HIPAA authorization waiver under 45 CFR 46.116(f) / 45 CFR 164.512(i); neither the waiver nor any consent pathway is recorded, and the record does not mark the absence at this location.

is_deidentified is populated with a method, but no de-identification standard is named (neither HIPAA Safe Harbor nor Expert Determination), no identifiers removed are enumerated, and participant_privacy.reidentification_risk is absent. The stated method - 'approaches that limit re-identification' - is a paraphrase rather than a specification, and imaging de-identification was still 'in process'. The record further notes that privacy_scan_tool and CTP-deid exist in the GitHub organization but does not state that either was applied to the released data, so no tool-to-artifact link closes the loop.

Deidentification-method appropriateness cannot be confirmed against the data type. The dataset carries high-risk quasi-identifiers - nursing flowsheets at high frequency, second-resolution waveform telemetry, EEG, DICOM pixel and header data, and DeGauss-geocoded OMOP Location entities - yet the documented protections are tokenization of note text plus controlled enclave access. Geocoding in particular increases rather than reduces re-identification risk and is listed under preprocessing_strategies with no corresponding protection in participant_privacy.

at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included=true, with PICU and NICU minors identified in human_subject_research.special_populations and subpopulations, but no assent procedures, guardian permission procedures or additional safeguards are described. The record discloses this in at_risk_populations.source_caveats rather than documenting the protections.

The dataset is US hospital PHI held under restricted confidentiality, yet regulatory_restrictions records no HIPAA determination, no limited-data-set/DUA characterization and no other_compliance entry. The record notes HIPAA and GDPR appear only as topics of a training workshop. A restricted clinical dataset with no stated regulatory basis leaves the access terms semantically incomplete.

No DOI or other persistent identifier is present anywhere in the record. The id field is 'https://chorus4ai.org/', which is identical to the page field: a project homepage, not a persistent identifier, and not a dataset-level landing page. Findability and sustainability therefore rest entirely on a resolvable but non-persistent project URL, against a dataset the record simultaneously describes as released and third-party shared.

distribution_formats enumerates five formats as if the dataset were distributed, while regulatory_restrictions states that 'Data are worked with inside a cloud enclave rather than distributed as files' and confidential_elements states the dataset 'is not openly downloadable'. The formats are therefore in-enclave working formats, not distribution formats, and no download_url exists. A reader taking distribution_formats at face value would form an incorrect expectation of how the data are obtained.

license_and_use_terms describes only a licensing agreement embedded in the AIM-AHEAD training-program registration form, and its source_caveats confirm no data use license is named for the dataset itself. Meanwhile third_party_sharing.is_shared=true and data_governance.access_review_process describes a general route via two email contacts. The consequence is that the terms governing the non-training-program access route are undocumented, so 'shared' and 'licensed' are not reconciled.

Two unreconciled volume disagreements propagate into the scored composition fields. Admissions: 50,000 (project website) versus 'over 45K unique admissions' (September 2025 webinar). Imaging: 7,642 admissions with radiology data (website) versus approximately 1,000 images available with de-identification in process (webinar). The record discloses both at description, instances.source_caveats and the top-level source_caveats and applies a stated source-ranking rule, which is good practice, but the headline instances.counts values (50000, 7642) are presented without inline qualification and are the values a downstream consumer will read.

instances.counts for OMOP rows is given as the exact integer 1600000000, which the record's own note identifies as its expansion of the rounded website figure '1.6 Billion Rows of EHR OMOP data' and 'not a count reported exactly by any source'. The disclosure is exemplary, but the serialized value implies ten significant figures of precision the source does not support.

There is no known_biases field, despite a title that reads 'Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI', keywords including 'social determinants of health', and a stated purpose of building AI models for clinical deployment. Relevant bias-adjacent content exists but sits in known_limitations (representativeness_limitation) and in a single clause of future_use_impacts about managing 'privacy and bias'; no bias is categorized, no taxonomy (BiasTypeEnum / AIO) is referenced, and no fairness analysis across the ICU/PICU/NICU or demographic strata is reported.

No version, version_access or errata field exists, and no persistent identifier anchors any release. The record describes a moving target (50,000 admissions now, 100,000 anticipated; imaging and EEG still in process; metadata for three of nine modalities 'planned') with no way to cite the state a given analysis used. updates.source_caveats confirms no update frequency or versioning policy. Sustainability is further exposed by the award period ending 2026-11-30 with no stated preservation commitment beyond it, and by the site banner recorded in notes.

The maintainer contact address 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu' contains an apparent misspelling of the harvard.edu domain. The record marks it 'address as printed on the site', so the transcription is faithful to the source rather than introduced here, but the contact as recorded is likely unroutable - which matters because this is the named project contact.

One external resource URL is recorded without a scheme ('www.bridge2ai.org/chorus') and is embedded in prose alongside 'AIM-AHEAD.net', while the remaining URLs (https://chorus4ai.org/, https://github.com/chorus-ai, https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema) are well formed and use plausible domains. Several external_resources entries name repositories (Chorus_SOP, chorus-mapping, chorus_waveform, chorus-extract-upload, privacy_scan_tool, CTP-deid, UF-Geocoding, CHoRUSReports) without individual URLs, so they are not directly resolvable.

labeling_strategies, splits and parts of tasks describe project intentions in the future tense ('a visualization and annotation environment will label data', 'will also provision a holdout test set') and are recorded in fields whose semantics imply realized dataset properties. The record flags this at labeling_strategies.source_caveats, splits.source_caveats and the top-level source_caveats, so the intent/state distinction is preserved - but a consumer reading splits alone would infer a holdout set exists when its size, composition and availability are unstated.

The documented processing pipeline (node2vec, DenseNet-121, contrastive co-embedding, HiDeF community detection, GPT-4/Gene Set AI naming) produces predicted cell maps, and the record states explicitly in known_limitations that 'It does not contain predicted cell maps, which will be added in future releases.' No software is named for producing or transforming the files that are actually distributed (SEC-MS and AP-MS result archives, the Perturb-seq cell atlas, the immunofluorescence image archives). FAIRSCAPE is named only as the RO-Crate packaging and provenance-metadata framework.

Version numbering is internally inconsistent: this June 2026 release is recorded as version '2.0', while version_access lists the earlier June 2025 and October 2025 releases at version '2.1'; the citation string ends 'V2'. A later release carrying a lower version number than its predecessors will mislead automated version resolution.

No variable-level metadata is provided. The `variables` slot is absent entirely, so no data dictionary, column definitions, or identifiers exist for the tabular content inside the distributed SEC-MS, AP-MS and Perturb-seq archives.

is_deidentified asserts a deidentification status and its rationale ('non-clinical (from tissue cultures) and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject') but names no deidentification method or standard. The rationale is semantically appropriate for immortalized and commercially sourced cell-line material, where no subject-level deidentification step was performed by the producers, but the record leaves the upstream basis unstated.

distribution_formats declares only the container format ('ZIP Archive', media_type application/zip) and the RO-Crate packaging standard. The formats of the files inside the archives (image format, mass-spectrometry table format, single-cell matrix format) and character encoding are not specified anywhere in the record.

Neither `anomalies` nor `missing_data_documentation` is populated. cleaning_strategies records only that single-cell CRISPR screen data 'were reported as undergoing quality control at the time of the CM4AI preprint', without stating outcomes, exclusions, or known quality defects in the released files.

No errata and no per-release change description. `updates` documents cadence (quarterly through November 2026) but not what changed between the October 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM) and this one; the reader must diff the two records to learn what was added.

The `download_url` slot is not populated; the platform access link is carried in distribution_formats.access_urls (https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C) with a note that the Data Access API is available. The information a consumer needs is present, but not in the slot a harvester would read.

Temporal fields are non-monotonic in two places: created_on (2025-02-27) is flagged by the record's own source_caveats as a Dataverse value carried unchanged across four successive releases, and five immunofluorescence file collections are listed as published 2026-07-15, after the dataset issued date of 2026-06-17. Both are disclosed rather than concealed.

Cell-line RRIDs (RRID:CVCL_0419 for MDA-MB-468, RRID:CVCL_B5P3 for KOLF2.1J) are valid Cellosaurus identifiers but appear only inside direct_collection prose, not in a resolvable identifier slot. No dataset-level RRID is claimed (none is required; the DOI serves that role).

Version ordering is internally inconsistent: this June 2026 release is declared version '2.0', while version_access lists the earlier June 2025 and October 2025 releases at version '2.1'. The citation string additionally identifies the deposit as 'V2'. A later release carrying a lower version string than its predecessors breaks the temporal ordering a consumer would use to select the newest data.

preprocessing_strategies and machine_annotation_tools document the MuSIC cell-map construction pipeline (node2vec, DenseNet-121 embeddings, contrastive co-embedding, HiDeF community detection, GPT-4/GSAI naming), but known_limitations states that this release 'does not contain predicted cell maps'. The processing actually applied to the released artifacts (mass-spectrometry search and elution-profile processing, immunofluorescence image QC, Perturb-seq alignment and guide assignment) is therefore undocumented.

third_party_sharing and raw_sources assert deposition in MassIVE, the Sequence Read Archive (via an NCBI BioProject), and Figshare, but no accession identifiers or URLs are given for any of these deposits, so the external raw data are named but not resolvable from this record.

File sizes are recorded only as human-readable strings inside file_collections descriptions ('3.8 GB', '113.3 KB') with total_size_bytes omitted; MD5 checksums are present but no byte counts. The record explains this in source_caveats, but machine-readable size metadata is still absent.

Temporal fields do not form a single clean ordering: issued 2026-06-17 precedes the 2026-07-15 publication date recorded for the three immunofluorescence file collections; created_on 2025-02-27 is acknowledged in source_caveats as carried unchanged from earlier releases; and updates promise quarterly augmentation 'through the end of the project in November 2026' while the funder record gives a project period ending 2026-08-31.

Three Q1 mandatory-field slots are unpopulated: variables (no variable-level metadata for the released tables), parent_datasets (prior releases are captured only as related_datasets with is_new_version_of), and regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level (a confidentiality determination is made narratively in confidential_elements but is not expressed as the schema's classification enum).

Ethics contact affiliation mismatch: Vardit Ravitsky is listed in creators with affiliation 'University of Montreal', while the ethical_reviews contact email for the same person is ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org and the description names the Hastings Center as a partner institution.

human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is false and no data_protection_impacts or formal reidentification_risk assessment is recorded, yet the record discloses donor-level attributes of the source material (a 51-year-old Black female metastatic breast cancer donor; a healthy male Northern European iPSC donor). The non-human-subjects determination is well supported for de-identified commercial cell lines, but the residual re-identification question for donor-derived genomic material is asserted rather than assessed.

machine_annotation_tools name four tools (node2vec, DenseNet-121, GPT-4, HiDeF) with informative descriptions but no version numbers or per-tool repository URLs; imputation_protocols, missing_data_documentation, annotation_analyses and errata are absent entirely.

The description states that this Beta release includes 'Perturb-seq data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment', but no MDA-MB-468 Perturb-seq file collection is listed among the ten archives (only cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_cell_atlas.zip and cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_raw_sra.zip are present). external_resources and confidential_elements record the MDA-MB-468 Perturb-seq deposition as embargoed, which contradicts its inclusion in the release contents.

The documented preprocessing pipeline (node2vec PPI embedding, HPA image embedding, contrastive co-embedding, community detection, GSAI annotation) produces cell maps, which known_limitations, anomalies and discouraged_uses all state are NOT included in this release. How the distributed processed_data packages (AP-MS, SEC-MS, Perturb-seq atlas) were themselves derived from raw acquisitions is not described.

No software is named that produced or transformed the released data. The named tooling falls entirely into excluded roles: node2vec, DenseNet-121, HiDeF, GPT-4/GSAI and the Cell Mapping Toolkit belong to a pipeline the record states produced cell maps not in this release; FAIRSCAPE produced the RO-Crate packaging and provenance metadata; the 10x Genomics kit, confocal microscope and pipetting robot are capture instrumentation; UVA Dataverse is the hosting platform.

Content-level file formats inside the distributed ZIP archives are not specified. distribution_formats declares only the container (ZIP, application/zip) and the metadata package (RO-Crate, application/ld+json); raw_data_sources gives 'Multi-channel confocal microscopy image files' without naming a standard (e.g. OME-TIFF, mzML, MTX/H5AD). No character encoding is stated.

No variable-level metadata is provided: the variables slot is absent entirely, and no data dictionary describes the columns of the distributed tabular components (AP-MS/SEC-MS result tables, Perturb-seq atlas). is_tabular: false is asserted at dataset level, but processed_data packages plainly contain tabular content.

No errata and no change description for this release. errata is absent; updates.update_details states only future cadence ('quarterly ... through the end of the project in November 2026') and carries no release or derivation information. The only change narrative in the record concerns an earlier release (related_datasets note on the June 2025 revision), not what June 2026 added over October 2025.

Version ordering is confusing: this June 2026 release is version 2.0, while version_access records the earlier June 2025 and October 2025 releases as version 2.1. A newer release carries a lower version string than its predecessors.
Stated update frequency 'quarterly' is not borne out by the release dates recorded: March 2025, June 2025, October 2025, then June 2026 — an eight-month interval between the last two.

Deidentification is asserted by rationale rather than by a named method: is_deidentified.deidentification_details argues the data 'cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject' because they are non-clinical tissue culture. No standard (Safe Harbor, expert determination) is invoked, while subpopulations.notes does disclose donor attributes for both lines (MDA-MB-468: 51-year-old black female, metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma; KOLF2.1J: healthy male Northern European donor).

The dedicated download_url slot is empty. Access is reachable only via the page landing URL plus platform access instructions carried in distribution_formats.notes (per-file direct download under a 1.9 GB limit; Dataverse Data Access API for programmatic access).

No release-level instance counts for the imaging modality. Project-level figures (53,788 immunofluorescent images, 7,023 proteins) are explicitly withheld in source_caveats as project-wide, and the per-condition protein count (464/563) is attributed to prior releases rather than to this one.

acquisition_methods states AP-MS was acquired 'under three conditions (untreated, paclitaxel treated, vorinostat treated)', while the release distributes AP-MS only for the two treated conditions. The acquisition text describes project-level acquisition rather than release contents, which is defensible but not signposted.

Version sequence is non-monotonic across the release series. This release (issued 2026-06-17) carries version '2.0', while the two EARLIER releases it supersedes are recorded at higher version numbers: June 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, 'version 2.1') and October 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, 'version 2.1'). The March 2025 release is 'version 1.4'. A consumer ordering releases by version string would place this release before its own predecessors.

The documented preprocessing pipeline does not correspond to the artifacts actually released. preprocessing_strategies and machine_annotation_tools describe cell-map construction (node2vec PPI embedding, DenseNet-121 image embedding, contrastive co-embedding, HiDeF community detection, GSAI/GPT-4 assembly naming), but known_limitations and discouraged_uses state that 'computed cell maps are not included in this release'. No preprocessing is documented for what is released: no mass-spectrometry search or quantification parameters for the AP-MS/SEC-MS packages, no image processing or segmentation for the IF archives, and no alignment/QC pipeline for the Perturb-seq atlas.

Embargo statements conflict with what is distributed. external_resources and third_party_sharing record the Perturb-seq depositions for both KOLF2.1J iPSCs and MDA-MB-468 as embargoed, yet the release distributes cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_cell_atlas.zip and cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_raw_sra.zip. Their stated sizes (30.2 KB and 73.3 KB) are implausibly small for a genome-scale atlas of 11,739 targeted genes or for raw SRA sequence data, suggesting pointer/manifest packages rather than data; the record does not say so. The same question arises for the SEC-MS and AP-MS packages (93.9 KB to 171.8 KB) against multi-GB image archives.

No variable-level metadata. The Q1 field set variables, resources and parent_datasets is entirely unpopulated, and regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is not asserted. For the tabular outputs (SEC-MS elution profiles, AP-MS interaction tables, Perturb-seq atlas) the absence of VariableMetadata leaves column semantics, units and value ranges undocumented, which is the semantic/statistical characterization axis of the Bridge2AI AI-readiness criteria the record itself invokes.

File sizes are not machine-readable. total_size_bytes is omitted at dataset level and total_bytes is omitted on all ten file_collections; sizes appear only as rounded free text inside notes ('Size reported by the repository as 4.6 GB'). The record documents this decision in source_caveats rather than presenting conversions of rounded figures as exact, which is sound practice, but the effect is that no program can compute the release size.

Bias documentation is narrow and no fairness analysis is present. known_biases carries two entries (selection_bias, sampling_bias) and no AIO or CROISSANT RAI term mappings. Measurement and technical bias is absent despite four measurement modalities where it dominates: antibody specificity and cross-reactivity in the IF imaging, abundance-dependent detection bias in AP-MS and SEC-MS, and variable knockdown efficiency in CRISPRi. The record's own known_limitations notes that the modalities 'interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap', a coverage bias that is not carried into known_biases.

The keyword 'mass spectroscopy' is an incorrect term for the methods used. The dataset employs mass spectrometry (AP-MS, SEC-MS), which the record names correctly everywhere else; 'spectroscopy' denotes a different class of technique and will match the wrong queries.

Several creator names are retained in surname-initial form rather than full personal names ('Axelsson U', 'Gao J', 'Lee YH', 'Sigaeva A', 'Ballllosero Navarro F'), and 'Ballllosero' contains a probable orthographic error (four consecutive 'l' characters). Most of these entries nonetheless carry ORCID iDs, which disambiguate them.

publisher is given only as the opaque CURIE 'ROR:0153tk833' with no human-readable label. The identifier resolves to the University of Virginia and is consistent with the DOI prefix and landing-page domain, so this is a readability rather than an accuracy defect.

Two disclosed source discrepancies remain unresolved in the record: the project end date (NIH RePORTER 2026-08-31 versus the Dataverse maintenance statement 'end of the project in November 2026'), and the affiliation of Andrej Sali (UCSD per the Dataverse release, UCSF per the Nature publication and preprint). In both cases the record states the conflict, names the competing sources and explains its resolution rule rather than silently picking one.
The citation string cites this release as 'V2' while the version field records '2.0'. Minor, but it compounds the version-sequence issue above for anyone matching a citation to a deposit version.

The processing documentation does not describe the distributed artifacts. All four preprocessing_strategies entries and the single labeling_strategies entry carry source_caveats stating that they are steps of the MuSIC pipeline whose cell-map outputs are 'not included in this release', one of them adding explicitly that 'this step was not applied to the artifacts distributed here'. What remains applicable to the released archives is one vague sentence ('Data generated by the acquisition modules undergo quality control before release') plus FAIRSCAPE RO-Crate packaging. Three of the five file_collections are typed collection_type: processed_data (AP-MS, SEC-MS, perturb-seq), so the released data were processed, yet no mass-spectrometry search or quantification step, no single-cell alignment or counting step, and no image-processing step is described for them.

No software is named in a producing or transforming role for the released data. The software the record does name falls outside that role: FAIRSCAPE client/framework performs RO-Crate packaging, provenance-metadata generation and input validation (packaging/metadata production and validation roles); the University of Virginia Dataverse is the hosting and serving platform; the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit is a capture reagent used at acquisition; and node2vec, the Human Protein Atlas embedding model, the contrastive co-embedding and community-detection steps, the Cell Mapping Toolkit (github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline) and the Integrative Modeling Platform all belong to pipelines the record itself states produced outputs that are not in this release, or that consume the release downstream. No used_software is attached to any property, and machine_annotation_tools and imputation_protocols are absent. No version number is given for any named software.

No variable-level metadata anywhere in the record. The variables slot is absent, is_tabular is absent, and no subsets block carries is_data_split or is_subpopulation flags. The release distributes AP-MS, SEC-MS and perturb-seq tables that are inherently tabular, but a reuser is given no column names, no units, no identifier scheme and no data dictionary for any of them.

The record omits publisher on the stated ground that 'The bundle names no publisher for the release', yet its own citation field prints 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2' in the publisher position of the citation, page resolves to dataverse.lib.virginia.edu, description says the data are 'archived in the University of Virginia Dataverse', and maintainers and retention_limit both name the UVA Dataverse (LibraData) as archival steward. The omission is therefore inconsistent with four other fields of the same record.

No anomalies documentation. The anomalies slot is absent and no substitute covers data-content quality issues: batch effects, failed or non-specific antibodies, discarded images, failed mass-spectrometry runs, low-complexity cells or filtered guides are nowhere discussed. known_limitations covers scope, coverage, embargo and expertise, and missing_data_documentation covers what is absent, but neither documents anomalies within the data that are present.

Deidentification is asserted without a formal method and without a residual-risk assessment. is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present is false and deidentification_details argue the material is non-identifiable because it derives from commercially available cell lines that 'cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject'. No recognised standard (Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, k-anonymity) is named and no identifiers_removed list is given. The rationale is also not tested against the record's own content: both lines are donor-derived and named, the record states MDA-MB-468 has public whole-genome sequencing data available, and the release distributes single-cell transcriptomic data, so genotype-based linkage is a risk the record asserts away rather than assesses.

Data formats are described only at the container level. distribution_formats gives 'ZIP archives containing RO-Crate packaged data files and metadata' with media_type application/zip, and conforms_to names JSON-LD, RDF-XML and JSON-Schema for the metadata and provenance layer, but no format is stated for the payload: the image files inside the three immunofluorescence archives, the AP-MS and SEC-MS tables and the perturb-seq matrices. description: Creator identifiers mix resolvable ORCIDs with locally minted, non-resolvable person IDs. Eight creators (Axelsson U, Chinn B, Fall J, Johannesson A, Khaliq H, Muralidharan M, Pan E, Polacco B, Zhang Y) carry identifiers of the form doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C#person-<surname>-<initial>, which are fragment identifiers on the dataset DOI and do not resolve to a person record. Names for these creators are surname-plus-initial only, which source_caveats acknowledges.

Distribution format variety is nominally one (ZIP) because ZIP is a container, not a data format. The record enumerates ten archives with checksums, sizes and publication dates but never states the internal formats (image format for the 12.6 GB of confocal IF data, matrix/h5ad format for perturb-seq, tabular format for SEC-MS and AP-MS elution and interaction data), so a reuser cannot determine what they will find inside before download.

Processing documentation is absent for the released data. None of preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses, imputation_protocols or missing_data_documentation is populated, even though seven of the ten archives are labelled collection_type: processed_data. The MuSIC pipeline and Cell Mapping Toolkit are described in notes and external_resources, but those produce the computed cell maps that this release explicitly excludes, so they do not document how the released processed files were derived from the raw acquisitions.

collection_timeframes states a 12-month collection period, which does not reconcile with the four-year phased IRB protocol also summarized in the same block (pilot collection begun November 2023, still ongoing November 2024) or with the six documented releases spanning November 2024 to May 2026. The record surfaces the conflict in its own source_caveats rather than concealing it, which is good documentation practice, but the collection window of the released data remains undetermined.

confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present is false, asserting no legally privileged data, while the same block's source_caveats and regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance both record that the underlying data are covered by a Certificate of Confidentiality that must be asserted against subpoenas. A CoC is a legal protection over the data, so the false flag reads more absolutely than the surrounding prose supports.

regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions states 'No export controls or other regulatory restrictions apply to the dataset', yet HIPAA de-identification rules, a Certificate of Confidentiality, PhysioNet credentialing requirements and a signed DUA all constrain the data and are documented in adjacent fields. The sweeping 'or other regulatory restrictions' clause contradicts the record's own compliance inventory.

keywords contains only four broad terms (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice). It omits the disease cohorts the dataset is organized around (voice disorders, Parkinson's/neurodegenerative, mood and psychiatric, respiratory), the modalities (speech, cough, breathing), the methods (spectrogram, MFCC, acoustic biomarker, machine learning) and the standards (BIDS) that a searcher would plausibly use.

variables declares only four columns (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames). These correctly document the join keys of the Parquet feature files, but the phenotype tables the record itself enumerates (confounders, demographics, diagnosis, enrollment, questionnaires, task metadata) have no variable-level entries here, and are covered only by the statement that JSON data dictionaries ship alongside the TSVs.

Several dedicated schema slots are unpopulated even though their substance is documented in prose elsewhere: publisher (PhysioNet is identified in citation, page, maintainers and third_party_sharing), download_url (access_urls and the DACO/credentialing process are given, and the absence of a file endpoint is explicitly and correctly explained by the access gating), is_tabular, imputation_protocols (no-imputation is stated in missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy), was_derived_from (derivation is carried by raw_data_sources and preprocessing_strategies), and media_type/encoding on the distribution formats. This costs machine-readability rather than human comprehension.

description: The RRID carried in the citation, RRID:SCR_007345, is well formed and resolves to PhysioNet, the hosting repository, rather than to the dataset itself. Using a repository RRID inside a dataset citation is a category slip: it identifies where the data sit, not the resource being cited.

The two renderings actually adopted into funders.grants are both well-formed NIH strings, and the malformed variant is quarantined in source_caveats rather than propagated, which is the correct handling; the underlying upstream inconsistency nonetheless remains unresolved.

The description lists pediatric voice and speech disorders among the five cohort categories recruited, while human_subject_research.special_populations and subpopulations state that pediatric participants are released as a separate dataset and that this release contains adults only. The two statements are reconcilable (five consortium cohorts versus one adult release) but the description does not make the scoping explicit at the point where it lists the cohorts.

The recording-count evidence is inconsistent across upstream sources: approximately 61,937 voice-derived recordings from 833 participants in the project documentation against per-feature counts on PhysioNet (32,522 pitch series, 29,278 spectrograms, 29,289 posteriorgram files). The record resolves this by preferring the higher-ranked source and declining to state a single recording total, which is defensible, but the audio-recording instance entry consequently carries no count.

collection_timeframes asserts a single unanchored figure ('The data were collected over a period of 12 months') while its own source_caveats records a four-year IRB study with pilot collection begun November 2023 and still ongoing November 2024, plus a feasibility window of 5 June to 28 July 2023. No start or end date is given for the released dataset's collection window, so a reuser cannot situate the data in time. The conflict is disclosed rather than concealed, but it remains unresolved.

The structured flag is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present is false, yet participant_privacy.reidentification_risk states that k-anonymization with k of 2 or more is not achieved and that re-identification by voice cannot be entirely excluded. The registered-access release ships spectrograms, Mel spectrograms and MFCCs, which are speaker-discriminative representations of the excluded waveform; the boolean therefore under-represents the residual risk the prose itself describes.

The description reports a consortium self-assessment of 100 percent on provenance ('transparent, traceable, interpretable, key actors identified') and 100 percent on FAIRness, while known_limitations records that the same self-assessment fails the data quality criterion under characterization and the domain-appropriate and associated criteria under sustainability. The record carries no was_derived_from or parent_datasets linkage, so the 100 percent provenance claim is not machine-evidenced within the datasheet itself.

The description enumerates five disease cohort categories including 'pediatric voice and speech disorders', but the record's scope is the adult dataset: human_subject_research.special_populations and related_datasets state that pediatric participants were released as a separate Bridge2AI-Voice Pediatric Dataset. subpopulations repeats the five-category list and then notes 'the adult dataset contains adult participants only'. A reader skimming the description could infer pediatric data is included in this release.

RRID:SCR_007345 appears inside the dataset citation string. The format is a valid RRID (RRID:SCR_XXXXX), but SCR_007345 identifies the PhysioNet resource, not this dataset; no dataset-level RRID is asserted and the record has no top-level rrid field.

Grant identifier renderings vary across the cited sources (OT2OD032720, 3OT2OD032720-01S1, 3OT2OD032720-01S3, 1OT2OD032720-01, and the malformed '3Tf-OTOD03272001S2' in a documentation footer). The two carried in funders.grants are both well-formed NIH identifiers and the variance is disclosed in source_caveats, but the malformed footer variant is quoted without being marked as a transcription error.

Only four keywords are supplied (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice) for a dataset spanning five clinical cohorts and dozens of conditions. No disease terms, modality terms (spectrogram, MFCC, cough, respiratory), standard ontology codes (SNOMED CT, ICD-10) or method terms appear in keywords, even though labeling_strategies states labels follow ICD-10 codes and instances carry B2AI_TOPIC / B2AI_SUBSTRATE ontology terms.

Structural containment fields resources and parent_datasets are absent, and variables enumerates only four columns (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames) for a release that includes phenotype tables covering confounders, demographics, diagnosis, enrollment, questionnaires and task metadata. No total_size_bytes, file_collections or total_file_count is given; per-feature file counts appear only inside source_caveats prose.

Tool documentation names the software used (sparc, openSMILE, Parselmouth, Praat, ppgs, Whisper Large, b2aiprep, senselab) with signal-processing parameters, but supplies no version numbers for any of them; 'Whisper Large' names a model size, not a pinned revision. tool_accuracy states transcriptions came from off-the-shelf models 'not audited for correctness', so no annotation quality metric is available. imputation_protocols is absent, though handling_strategy states no imputation is applied.

Demographic sub-populations are named by axis (age, gender, sex, ethnicity, socioeconomic status) and their skew is described qualitatively, but no counts or distributions per stratum are given, and the inclusion and exclusion criteria are referred to ('the corresponding inclusion and exclusion criteria') without being enumerated. Only English-only and adult-only exclusions are stated concretely, via known_limitations.

known_biases uses four taxonomy-conformant bias_type values with clear descriptions, but only one of the four carries a mitigation_strategy and only one carries affected_subsets. No quantitative fairness analysis (subgroup counts, parity metrics) and no explicit AIO ontology mappings are present; fairness is treated qualitatively via future_use_impacts and discouraged_uses.

Identifier rendering is inconsistent: doi is the bare string '10.13026/8xbn-nq66' while id and version_access.latest_version_doi and related_datasets.target_dataset use the 'doi:' CURIE prefix. There is no top-level publisher field, although PhysioNet is identified as host in citation, maintainers and data_governance.stewardship_roles.

keywords contains only four broad terms (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice). It falls below the five-keyword expectation and, more importantly, covers only the domain: none of the disease cohorts (voice, neurological, mood/psychiatric, respiratory disorders), none of the acoustic methods (spectrogram, MFCC, articulatory coding, phonetic posteriorgram) and none of the data modalities documented at length elsewhere in the record are reachable by keyword search.

No download_url slot is populated. Access is nevertheless operationally resolvable: the PhysioNet version-specific landing page, the registered-access procedure, the DACO review route and the Synapse controlled-access URLs are all given.
distribution_formats names formats and even individual file names but records no media_type (MIME) and no character encoding for the TSV and JSON products.

data_protection_impacts states plainly that no analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted, while participant_privacy.reidentification_risk concedes that voice is inherently identifying and that k-anonymity with k>=2 is not achieved. A formal DPIA is the instrument that would normally be expected given that admitted residual risk, even though the consortium substitutes an ethicist review of sensitive fields and a published memorandum justifying controlled access.

sensitive_elements declares sensitive_elements_present: true for race/ethnic origin, sexual orientation and socioeconomic/health information, while the notes on the same block state that fields encoded as sensitive in the REDCap data dictionary were removed before release along with household income, mental health status and traumatic life experiences. A reader cannot determine from these two statements which sensitive attributes survive into the published feature-only release.

is_tabular is not set although the release distributes tab-separated phenotype tables, static features and audio quality metrics alongside the Parquet tensors, and the variables block enumerates tabular columns.

No structured imputation_protocols block is present. The substance is supplied instead by missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy, which states that no imputation is performed and that a missingness table accompanies the release, so the concept is documented even though the dedicated slot is empty.

Temporal inconsistency in the collection window. collection_timeframes states the data were collected 'over a period of twelve months' (and known_limitations repeats 'approximately twelve months'), but the same field records accrual across releases published November 2024 (306 participants), version 2.0 April 2025 (+136) and version 3.0.0 December 2025 (+391), a span of roughly twenty-five months of accrual. No absolute collection start or end date is given anywhere in the record, so the twelve-month figure cannot be reconciled with the release timeline.

data_protection_impacts states plainly that 'No analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted', while the same record documents biometric voice data, psychiatric and cognitive-impairment cohorts, an explicit statement that k-anonymity with k>=2 is not achieved, and an acknowledgement that voice can never be fully de-identified. The absence of a formal DPIA is honestly disclosed and partly offset by ethicist review of sensitive fields and the published memorandum 'Ethical Justification for Controlled Access to Raw Voice Data Samples', but the substantive gap remains for a dataset of this sensitivity.

The final errata entry asserts 'No formal erratum is published', directly following three concrete erratum entries describing spectrogram reprocessing in v2.0.0, an authorship correction in v2.0.1 and Parquet repairs plus diagnosis back-fill in v3.1.0. The intended meaning is presumably that no standalone erratum document exists and corrections are carried in the changelog, but as written the list contradicts itself.

The standards-conformance claims do not cover the artifacts actually released. conforms_to states BIDS v1.9.0 applies to 'the audio dataset layout and the phenotype folder organization rather than to the Parquet feature files of the published feature-only release' — that is, not to the dense features that constitute the release — while conforms_to_schema points to the LinkML data-sheets schema, which governs this datasheet rather than the data files. Column-level structure for the released files rests on the per-file JSON data dictionaries, which are documented but are not a registered standard.

regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions asserts that 'No export controls or other regulatory restrictions apply to the dataset or to individual instances', while regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance in the same block documents a Certificate of Confidentiality that must be asserted against subpoenas, and hipaa_compliant is set to 'compliant'. The two senses (trade/export control versus privacy regulation) are distinguishable, but the blanket phrase 'or other regulatory restrictions' overreaches.

Discovery metadata is thin relative to the record's own content. keywords holds only four generic terms (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice) for a dataset the description characterizes as spanning five disease cohorts (voice, neurological and neurodegenerative, mood and psychiatric, respiratory, controls) and that notes 22 acoustic tasks. None of the cohort names, modality terms (spectrogram, MFCC, articulatory, cough, respiration) or coding systems referenced elsewhere (ICD-10, B2AI_TOPIC, B2AI_SUBSTRATE) appear as keywords.

Two hierarchical schema fields named by Q1 are unpopulated: resources and parent_datasets. The underlying information is present in other fields — was_derived_from describes the raw audio and REDCap origin, and related_datasets carries six typed relationships with DOIs including is_new_version_of and is_version_of — so this is a placement gap rather than missing knowledge, but it reduces mandatory-field coverage to roughly 86 percent.

Bias documentation is taxonomy-aligned but the fairness analysis is qualitative only. Two of four known_biases entries (measurement_bias, annotation_bias) carry no mitigation_strategy, and no quantitative demographic distributions, subgroup counts or fairness metrics appear anywhere: subpopulations names the demographic axes (age, gender, sex, ethnicity, socioeconomic status) and states the sample is 'skewed by site and by demographic factors' without reporting the skew. No AIO ontology term URIs are attached to the bias types.

keywords contains only four terms (voice, health, biomarkers, bridge2ai), below the five-term threshold, and covers domain and program affiliation only. No methods terms (machine learning, acoustic features, spectrogram, speech), no condition terms (Parkinson's disease, dysphonia, depression, chronic cough) and no modality terms appear, despite all being described at length elsewhere in the record.

No variables field is present. The record documents that every released table is paired with a JSON data dictionary keyed by column name, and names the tables, but supplies no variable-level identifiers, types or descriptions in the datasheet itself. A reuser must fetch the release to learn what any column means.

at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included is false, while the subsets enumerate participants with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, other dementias, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and alcohol or substance use disorder. These are conventionally treated as populations with potentially impaired decisional capacity. The special_protections text partially reconciles the flag by recording that enrollment required the ability to provide informed consent for oneself in English, but the boolean as stated understates the cohort composition.

is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present is false, while participant_privacy.reidentification_risk and is_deidentified.deidentification_details both state that k-anonymization with k greater than or equal to two is not achieved for the released tables. HIPAA Safe Harbor does not require k-anonymity, so the two claims are reconcilable under that framing, but an unqualified false flag sits awkwardly beside an explicit statement of residual re-identification risk in the released files.

updates.frequency states a semi-annual cadence, while the release dates recorded in version_access and distribution_dates run January 2025, April 2025, August 2025, December 2025 and May 2026 - approximately quarterly through 2025. The record discloses this discrepancy itself in updates.source_caveats and attributes the semi-annual figure to the project documentation.

data_protection_impacts.impact_details describes an ethicist review of sensitive fields and a published memorandum justifying controlled access, while its source_caveats records that the healthsheet answers 'No' to whether an impact analysis on data subjects was conducted. The tension is disclosed rather than concealed, and the substantive activities described do constitute an impact assessment in effect.

No download_url field is populated. The platform link is nonetheless available: distribution_formats[].access_urls give the versioned PhysioNet URL and the Synapse controlled-access URL, page resolves to the same PhysioNet record, and data_governance.access_review_process gives step-by-step access instructions for both tiers.

is_tabular is not set, although the release is substantially tabular (TSV phenotype tables and static features, Parquet feature tables with a documented row granularity of one row per unique recording).

The record mitigates the claim by requiring capacity to consent in English, but the boolean as stated understates the population risk profile and is in tension with the subsets it describes.

The element therefore both claims and disclaims an impact assessment.

The keywords field contains only four terms (voice, health, biomarkers, bridge2ai) for a dataset whose subsets enumerate more than fifty clinical conditions across four disease cohorts and whose description names seventeen acoustic tasks and thirteen validated instruments. The controlled vocabulary does not carry the topical coverage the rest of the record demonstrates, which depresses findability by topic.

Variable-level metadata is described narratively (every table is 'paired with a JSON data dictionary keyed by column name') but no variables element is emitted, so column semantics are not machine-readable from the datasheet itself.

The scoping difference (released tier versus source tier) is stated elsewhere but not inside the confidential_elements element.

Hosting and maintenance are attributed to PhysioNet / MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology in maintainers and regulatory_restrictions, while the project documentation is quoted as placing hosting with the Health Data Nexus at the University of Toronto. The record resolves the conflict in favour of the PhysioNet record and attributes the other statement to v1.0, so the residual risk to a reader is small.

No aggregate recording count and no byte sizes are recorded. instances.counts is populated for participants (833) but deliberately omitted for recordings because the preferred source gives only per-feature counts; total_size_bytes and file_collections.total_bytes are absent throughout, so a prospective user cannot size a download.

version_access.latest_version_doi is doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42, an identifier that appears nowhere else in the record and that conflicts with the record's own DOI for the latest listed version (3.1.0 = doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66, listed in versions_available and in doi/id/citation).

keywords contains only four generic terms (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice). is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present is false while the same block states that 'K-anonymization with k of two or more is not achieved' and participant_privacy.reidentification_risk states that voice cannot be fully de-identified. The record discloses the provenance of the figure but still asserts it for 3.1.0.

No data-standard conformance is asserted for this release: conforms_to is absent and conforms_to_schema names the metadata record's own schema (w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema) rather than a standard the data conforms to. source_caveats explains that earlier releases were converted to BIDS v1.9.0 but that the 3.1.0 features/metadata/phenotype layout states no such conformance.

Several schema slots that the rubric reads are unused even though equivalent content exists elsewhere: download_url (access URLs appear only inside distribution_formats and data_governance.access_review_process), is_tabular, character encoding on any distributed file, Parquet media_type, imputation_protocols, and data_governance.committee_contact (the DACO mailbox appears only in notes).

version_access.latest_version_doi is 'doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42', a DOI that appears nowhere else in the record and does not match the DOI the record itself gives for its latest version. regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant is asserted as 'compliant' and other_compliance states HIPAA de-identification rules were applied, while the record's own regulatory_restrictions.source_caveats quotes the Data Transfer and Use Agreement describing the transferred data as personally identifiable information under OMB M-07-16 that is 'not covered under HIPAA, FERPA, or similar laws'. The abstention is correct and well-reasoned, but leaves the release without a declared data standard.
